s:
What were the main trade routes during the rule of Kakatiyas?
I. Orugallu - Tripurantakam - Nellore
II. Dwarasamudra - Bellary - Orugallu
III. Motupalli - Tripurantakam - Bellary
IV. Palnadu - Nalgonda - Nekarikallu - Orugallu
Select the correct answer using the codes given below?
x: Orugallu was the main centre of domestic trade in the Kakatiya period; Kridabhiramam mentions the Motupalli-Tripurantakam-Bellary route and the Palanadu-Nalgonda-Nekarikallu-Orugallu route.

s: Identify the incorrect pair in the stories of foreigners of Vijayanagara period?
o: Abdul Razak : Describes the conditions during the reign of Devaraya II
Caesar Frederick : Wrote the situation in Vijayanagara after the Battle of Rakshasa Tangadi
Nikitin : Achyuta came as a pilgrim during the rule of Devaraya
x: Nikitin visited during the reign of Virupaksha Raya-II, not Devaraya.

source: latestpyqs RRR AP History Previous Papers (b2p3) p8
s: Which Vijayanagara rulers allowed the Jesuits to build churches in Nellore and Chandragiri?
x: Venkatapati Raya-II gave permission to build a Christian church at Chandragiri. He allowed the Portuguese to build a church in his empire.

s:
Match the following mentioned texts with their authors?
a. Prajnaparamita
b. Samaya Sara
c. Lilavati parinayam
d. Katantra vyakaranam
I. Konda Kundacharya
II. Sarvavarma
III. Acharya Nagarjuna
IV. Kuthuhala
Select the correct answer using the codes given below?
x: Prajnaparamita - Acharya Nagarjuna, Samayasara - Konda Kundacharya, Lilavati Parinayam - Kutuhala, Katantra Vyakarana - Sarvavarma.

s: Mitakshara written by Vignesvara in the court of Chalukya Vikramaditya-VI is a ?
x: Vijnanesvara wrote the Dharmasastra Mitakshara based on the Yajnavalkya Smriti. Hindu property inheritance in India still follows Mitakshara.

s: In January 1565 Battle of Tallikota was fought between whom?
o: Vijayanagara Empire and Sultans of Deccan
x: In 1565 four Bahmani successor kingdoms (Golconda, Ahmednagar, Bidar, Bijapur) formed an alliance and declared war on the Vijayanagara Empire. It is also known as the Rakshasi Tangadi or Bannihatti War.
